cases.prompt:
Repair the supplied forecasting/replenishment project according to CONTRACT.md. Deliver the complete deliverable.pyz, maintainable source and concise handoff. Work directly in this project without delegation.

Repair the demand-forecast/replenishment prototype; release deliverable.pyz,
maintainable source, and a concise handoff with actual validation results.
Python 3 standard library only. Invocation from any working directory:
  python deliverable.pyz INPUT_DIRECTORY --output OUTPUT_JSON
INPUT_DIRECTORY contains train.csv, validation.csv, future.csv, inventory.csv (UTF-8 CSV).
train/validation: date,item,is_open,demand; future: date,item,is_open;
inventory: item,stock,buffer. Dates are ISO dates; is_open is 0 or 1;
demand/stock/buffer are nonnegative integers. Item names are exact nonempty Unicode text.
Required named columns may be reordered; extra metadata columns, legal CSV quoting
and CRLF/LF are supported. Future/validation items all have training and inventory.
Each item has all seven weekdays in training and at least one open observation;
dates are unique per item in each split. Compare all three supplied strategies:
  weekday: mean training demand for the item's weekday, including closed observations;
  open: mean demand over the item's open training observations if is_open=1, else zero;
  last: demand on that item's latest training date, independent of is_open.
Apply training-only predictors to the separate validation rows. Choose globally lowest
mean squared error (MSE), equally weighted across validation rows; exact ties choose
the lexicographically first strategy name. Never train on validation/future labels.
The released forecast must execute the selected strategy, replacing stale release metadata.
For each future row, order=max(0,forecast+buffer-stock); rows are independent planning
scenarios, with no inventory carry. Include every future row, sorted by date then item.
Write JSON {selected:STRATEGY,validation_mse:{last:NUMBER,open:NUMBER,weekday:NUMBER},
plan:[{date:DATE,item:EXACT_TEXT,forecast:NUMBER,order:NUMBER},...]}.
Numbers may be integer/float with 1e-8 absolute error. Validation losses, selection and
actual released predictions/quantities must agree. Existing prototype/scores/config
are development material, not acceptance evidence.

parts.text:
Delivered `deliverable.pyz`, repaired source in `main.py`, reproducible packaging in `build.py`, regression tests in `test_delivery.py`, and a concise `HANDOFF.md`.

**Repairs:** proper CSV parsing, training-only predictors, global validation MSE, exact tie-breaking, forecasts using the selected strategy, and independent per-row replenishment.

**Verification:** all 8 test groups passed against the final rebuilt archive, running outside the project directory. Coverage includes all three strategy winners, Unicode/quoted CSV, reordered columns, fractional means, ties, and 12 seeded multi-item datasets.

Supplied sample results:

| Strategy | Validation MSE |
|---|---:|
| last | 214.28571428571428 |
| **open — selected** | **0** |
| weekday | 71.42857142857143 |

All six sample forecasts and orders matched hand calculations.

```sh
python /path/to/deliverable.pyz INPUT_DIRECTORY --output OUTPUT_JSON
```

No commits were created; unrelated files were preserved.

Repair this manifest-driven file delivery project. Deliver deliverable.pyz,
maintainable source and a concise tested handoff; Python 3 standard library only.
Invocation: python deliverable.pyz INPUT_DIRECTORY --output OUTPUT_ZIP
INPUT_DIRECTORY contains manifest.json {files:[{source:RELATIVE_PATH,target:ZIP_PATH},...]}.
Source paths are relative to that directory; targets are distinct relative forward-slash
ZIP paths; all paths are nonempty and contain no traversal/absolute components.
Legal names include Unicode, spaces, dots and commas; nested paths and duplicate source
basenames in different directories are supported. Inputs may be binary, empty or text.
Copy the exact bytes of every specified source to its exact target, without text decoding.
The ZIP also contains _bundle_index.json {files:[{path:TARGET,bytes:INTEGER},...]} sorted
by target Unicode order. Other payload files must not be included; directory entries are
allowed. manifest order does not affect the delivered logical tree or sorted index.
The zipapp must run from an arbitrary working directory with only its own archive,
Python and the supplied inputs. Verify the actual resulting ZIP, not just zipapp exit.

Repair the supplied project according to CONTRACT.md. Deliver the complete deliverable.pyz, maintainable source and concise handoff. Work directly in this project without delegation.

Repair this SQLite stock-batch import project. Deliver deliverable.pyz,
maintainable source and concise tested handoff; Python 3 standard library only.
Invocation: python deliverable.pyz INPUT_CSV --db DATABASE --output REPORT_JSON
CSV is UTF-8 with named item,delta,unit_cost_cents columns, reordered/extra metadata
columns and all legal CSV quoting/CRLF/LF supported. item is exact nonempty Unicode
text including quotes, commas and embedded newlines; delta is signed integer, cost
nonnegative integer. Apply rows in order in one atomic transaction. Existing stock rows
add delta and replace cost; new rows start quantity zero plus delta. Every resulting
quantity must be nonnegative. On success exit 0 and JSON {success:true,processed:N}.
On the first insufficient-stock record, roll back the entire batch, exit 2 and JSON
{success:false,error:{code:"INSUFFICIENT_STOCK",record:ONE_BASED_DATA_RECORD,item:TEXT}}.
The existing SQLite schema has stock(item TEXT PRIMARY KEY,quantity INTEGER NOT NULL
CHECK(quantity>=0),unit_cost_cents INTEGER NOT NULL). Preserve all user tables, indexes,
triggers, prior rows and their semantics; execute ordinary INSERT/UPDATE so existing
audit triggers record actual changes. No replacement of the database or stock table.
Consume the exact supplied DB path and persist success across physical reopening.
Provide the real packaged CLI and test both success and explicit atomic-error behavior.

CREATE TRIGGER stock_insert AFTER INSERT ON stock BEGIN INSERT INTO stock_events(item,before_quantity,after_quantity) VALUES(new.item,NULL,new.quantity);END
CREATE TRIGGER stock_update AFTER UPDATE ON stock BEGIN INSERT INTO stock_events(item,before_quantity,after_quantity) VALUES(new.item,old.quantity,new.quantity);END
